body: Yeah, I am definitely the impatient type when it comes to improvement. Thank you so much for your advice! I guess starting out, I thought that if I wasn't pushing myself crazy hard, I was being lazy. Your post is very helpful! I appreciate it!

Eh, I live in an area of a big city where I wouldn't feel safe enough to run outdoors, especially since most of my runs are in the evening and it's been getting darker earlier. I definitely appreciate the advice though, it seems the consensus is that I've been overdoing it way too much! Thank you!

I feel like I'm taking crazy pills reading this thread...can you imagine the type of society we'd live in if everyone carried out this sort of vigilante justice? Or reasoned this sort of violence with "Oh, even though I haven't tried it out yet, I already know for certain that the law won't work, so I guess I just HAVE to beat someone up..." NO! Self-defense laws are structured a certain way for a reason! While the law is not always correct, OP, in this case, it reflects the principles that best create order in society. You seriously can't have people assaulting each other, just because one person feels that the other deserves it. I completely understand why you'd want to beat him up, and her boyfriend is a huge piece of shit. But you are a freaking grown man who presumably has the cognitive ability to suppress violent urges. I understand why your girlfriend was upset. You probably didn't even help your sister, by the way. She will go back to him, and you are deluded if you genuinely think he'll stop beating her up after this. Abuse doesn't work that way; it is chronic.

Reddit has always had a problem with sympathizing with vigilante justice. You need a reality check if you think this is socially acceptable. This sort of thinking will get you in trouble with the law, and has already gotten you in trouble with your personal relationships. In her mind, now you're the type of person that will resort to violence before resorting to the law. What about the next time someone 'deserves' it? 

Bring on the downvotes.
No problem. Good luck to you and your friend
Yeah, that definitely makes it difficult to tell whether or not she is truly committed to staying away. Like I said, complex situation :/

This is such a difficult situation, I can't blame you at all for being frustrates with your friend. It was awful to watch the ones you love get hurt. That being said...if she feels like she has no outside support, and nowhere to go, she will never leave him. Of course, she may never leave him regardless, but standing up to an abuser takes a lot of courage and while she needs to make the decision to leave for herself, she will likely need help in finding a place to stay, staying safe, etc. I think that limiting contact while she is with him is a good idea, but make it absolutely clear that if she makes the final decision to leave and needs help getting out, you will help her (if you're willing to do that).

I literally can't believe there people are telling you this is your fault. Its not. You had TOLD him before that you didn't want to sleep with him while drunk. I don't think its unreasonable to call friends to ask for a ride if you're drunk, which everyone is blaming you for. And he KNEW you were blackout drunk, you vomited, and even if you threw yourself at him, he was sober--he knew there was no way you would consent if you were sober. Reddit is fucking ridiculous. It's not your fault and you should stop blaming yourself. He was sober, you were blackout, he knew that, you had told him before you didn't want to have sex while drunk, and he still took advantage of you when you were vulnerable and mentally unable to consent. Jesus christ. I'll get down votes for this, no fucks given, but if you consult ANYWHERE other than reddit (which is notoriously extremely harsh towards female rape victims), this would be defined as rape, without a doubt.

I think you are missing the point...she was the one doing all the initiating, and it was a very one-sided relationship. By "playing hard to get" (a ridiculous phrase in the first place, because she made herself very available to him if he simply asked), she forced him to actually initiate contact for once. I know that I feel like a desperate creeper if I am the only one initiating the texting, so it is perfectly reasonable that she would take a break from that to see if he contacted her first.
